news.title: These Gen Z-ers are choosing ETFs over sports bets. How younger investors told us they’re building wealth.
news.description: Gen Z is entering the market unusually young, with easier access to investing than previous generations but vastly different amounts of money to put to work.
news.author: Genna Contino

copy.hook: Same $50: one game-night bet, or a slice of 500 companies?
copy.explain: An ETF (a basket fund) is one share that holds many companies at once. An S&P 500 fund, for example, owns about 500 U.S. firms. A sports bet is settled in one night, win or lose. Gen Z is starting young, so even small amounts get more years to compound (earn gains on gains).
copy.takeaway: Time in the market does more for small amounts than any single lucky bet.
copy.question: Gen Z readers: did your first $100 go to an ETF, a bet, or neither?
